candidates.title: Heavy fighting erupts in Haiti as armed forces fight gangs to regain control of key corridor
candidates.originator: Haitian National Police (PNH), via Associated Press
candidates.why_new: PNH says at least 34 suspected gang members killed 19.11 in a Martissant operation run with a 'task force' that includes personnel from Vectus Global, a private security firm -- first significant operation in 5 years to contest that corridor. Names the same private-contractor / parallel-command question Cadre 7's N-001 and Cadre 509 cell 03 already track, in a new incident. Corroborating but not independently verified here: Juno7 (riotimesonline.com/haiti-martissant-drone-offensive-reported, 19.11, drone use, no official toll) and Spanish-language wire pickups (primicias.ec, elcomercio.com, noticiasrcn.com, democrata.es) that all appear to relay the same PNH/AP account rather than add an independent originator.

candidates.title: Haiti formalizes security agreement with El Salvador following troop deployment
candidates.originator: Government of Haiti -- Council of Ministers (Facebook announcement)
candidates.why_new: Haiti's Council of Ministers announced 18.11 that it approved a 'cooperation agreement' with El Salvador, called a new stage in bilateral security cooperation. Directly on-topic for Cadre 7 N-001 ('Is the Salvadoran surge under any written instrument?') and its falsifier (publication of a decree/bilateral agreement/exchange of letters) -- but NOTE: this is an announcement that an agreement was approved, not a published text. No duration, command structure, or troop number is given in this report. Whether this counts as movement toward the falsifier, short of it, or something else is a desk call, not made here.

candidates.title: A model for future peace operations? Lessons from the Gang Suppression Force in Haiti
candidates.originator: Sophie Rutenbar / Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime (GI-TOC)
candidates.why_new: Full-length NGO analytical report on GSF performance since the 18.10 ambush, not previously in any ledger. Snippet seen mentions a Gros Morne incident ('gang members massacred around a dozen civilians only hours after a GSF operation killed three') that is not dated precisely in what was retrieved and may itself be a distinct candidate worth checking once the desk reads the full PDF. Worth a read for Cadre 7's end-state cell and Cadre 509's command/end-state cells -- this engine has not attempted to extract or verify its specific claims.
